claims.claim: Tuples are immutable sequences in Python.
A comma, not parentheses alone, forms a tuple; `()` is the empty-tuple display.
A one-item tuple requires a trailing comma, such as `(value,)`.
Comma-separated values can be packed into a tuple and unpacked into matching assignment targets.
Basic sequence unpacking requires the number of targets to match the number of values.
Assigning a new tuple to a name is rebinding and differs from assigning to an existing tuple position.
